batchName: Early Republic: The Conflict of the Orders - Toward Resolution (450-367 BCE) - Latin words
chapterName: Early Republic: The Conflict of the Orders - Toward Resolution (450-367 BCE)
description: Written by hand from the chapter text: the Latin words it explains

questions.question: What did Brennus mean by “Vae victis!”?
questions.explanation: He threw his sword onto the scales when the Romans complained about rigged weights.

questions.question: The Romans took Veii through a cuniculus. What was it?
questions.explanation: They dug it through the soft volcanic rock under the city.
questions.sourceQuote: They dug a tunnel (*cuniculus*) through the soft volcanic rock

questions.question: What were the anseres that woke Marcus Manlius?
questions.explanation: The guards and dogs slept, but the geese honked.
questions.sourceQuote: but the sacred geese (*anseres*) of Juno honked.

questions.question: What was the ager publicus that the land law limited?
options: Public land owned by the Roman state
The common pasture of the patricians
questions.explanation: Rich landowners had grabbed huge areas of it; the law capped each person at about 120 hectares (300 acres).
questions.sourceQuote: The land law targeted public land (*ager publicus*) owned by the Roman state.

questions.question: After Veii fell, its people received civitas sine suffragio. What was that?
options: Citizenship without the right to vote
The right to elect their own consuls
questions.explanation: It bound the newly conquered city closer to Rome.
questions.sourceQuote: by giving its people citizenship without the right to vote (*civitas sine suffragio*).

questions.question: The dictator Publius Manlius Capitolinus chose a plebeian magister equitum. What was that?
options: His deputy, the “master of the horse”
questions.explanation: Picking a plebeian deputy angered the patricians.
questions.sourceQuote: angered patricians by picking a plebeian deputy, a "master of the horse" (*magister equitum*).

questions.question: What was the dies Alliensis?
options: The ill-omened anniversary of the Allia, 18 July
The day the Gauls left Rome
The festival of the sacred geese
questions.explanation: The day of the defeat at the Allia became a day when public business stopped.
questions.sourceQuote: Its anniversary, 18 July, became an ill-omened day (*dies Alliensis*, "the day of the Allia").

questions.question: Livy called some later tribunes mancipia nobilium. What did he mean?
questions.explanation: Once in power, the plebeian leaders joined the patricians in a new nobility and forgot the poor.
questions.sourceQuote: and Livy called some tribunes “slaves of the nobility” (*mancipia nobilium*).
